outlook.statement: recovery and crushing has been increased gradually and is expected to further improve in the coming seasons

There is adequate production capacity and steps are being taken to improve the cost efficiency. The impact of the above measures is also reflecting in the Audited accounts of the Company for the financial year under review. These measures are expected to go a long way in improving the performance of the Company.

The Company continued to focus on cane development activities, comprising of varietal replacement with proven high sugared varieties, change in pattern of sowing, ratoon management, encouraging use of Bio – fertilizers, Bio-pesticides, soil testing activities, crop protection etc. and modern agricultural practices due to which the recovery and crushing is expected to improve in the coming season.

UDL is also taking necessary steps, to expand its distillery capacity from 40 KLPD to 160 KLPD, to capitalize on the government's ethanol blending focus and increased production of ENA in the state of Uttarakhand.

Growing demand, favorable government policies, and the shift toward renewable energy make ethanol a strategic opportunity for business growth, environmental sustainability, and reduced carbon emissions.
Climate Change can have adverse impact on business and not having a correct strategy or its right implementation will severely affect the business continuity.
Target to determine details of total scope 3 emission and its intensity in the meantime.

Global growth is projected to slow to 2.5 percent in 2026, from 2.9 percent in 2025—the lowest rate since the COVID-19 pandemic—amid weaker prospects for economies dependent on energy imports and those directly affected by hostilities. Activity is expected to firm in 2027–28 as energy supplies recover, monetary easing resumes, and trade strengthens.

India's growth being driven by strong domestic demand and consistent government spending. These factors have supported stable employment and helped contain inflation, which is expected to full 3.93% (retail inflation rate) and 4.78% (consumer food inflation rate) well within the target of Reserve Bank of India.
India's manufacturing GVA growth strengthened with 7.72% in Q1 and 9.13% in Q2 of FY 2025-26; government aims to increase manufacturing contribution to GDP from 17% to 25% by 2030.
Global sugar production forecast down 1.2 million tons to 181.29 million tons in 2025-26; India production forecast to recover 3.6 million tons to 33.6 million tons.

Ethanol blending reached 20% average in December 2025, five years ahead of schedule; draft amendments for E85/E100 and higher blends (E22, E25, E27, E30) indicate policy direction for higher ethanol penetration.

Ethanol capacity has scaled to ~2000 crore litres with additional 400 crore litres expected by FY27; demand under E20 only ~1100 crore litres, leading to structural overcapacity and utilization of 65-75% for next three years.
Sector transitioning into consolidation phase; focus shifting to brownfield capex, debottlenecking, and operational efficiencies.
